text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.

LONDON - Britain's leading blue-chip index charged further into record ground as investors cheered a signal from the Bank of England that its quarter-point interest rate hike was likely to be the last for a while, strategists and dealers said. The FTSE 100 closed at 5,086.8, up 60.6 points, or 1.21 percent.

FRANKFURT - An overnight rally on Wall Street lifted the mood on the wary German share market, helping to push prices to healthy gains. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,414.35, up 78.96 points, or 1.82 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,428.08, up 63.83 points, or 1.46 percent.
PARIS - French shares finished higher after tracking a rise on Wall Street to record levels. The CAC-40 index closed at 3,056.34, up 19.25 points, or 0.63 percent.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed sharply higher, powered by firmer U.S. financial markets, a strong dollar and positive company results, dealers said. The Swiss market index closed at 5,922.1, up 110.0 points, or 1.89 percent.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed lower, with the key market index finishing below the 19,500 mark for the first time since May 1. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19,475.85, down 226.22 points, or 1.15 percent.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index continued its record-breaking run, climbing 131.67 points, or 0.80 percent to a record close of 16,673.27. The Hang Seng index closed at 16,673.27, up 131.67 points, or 0.80 percent.

SYDNEY - Bellwether Broken Hill Pty Co. Ltd. led the Australian share market to a lower close as traders expressed concern about the costs and direction of its mineral division. The all ordinaries index closed at 2,717.7, down 9.4 points, or 0.34 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Strong foreign buying and futures-driven trade hoisted South African shares to new highs, pushing the all-share index above the 7,600 level for the first time in big turnover trade. The all-share index closed at 7,614.4, up 67.6 points, or 0.90 percent. The all gold index closed at 967.1, up 10.1 points, or 1.06 percent, while the industrial index closed at 9,314.2, up 67.1 points, or 0.73 percent.
